observer.integration: not integrated into the product candidate; explicit diagnostic startup adapter is required

reviewed_invariants: The wrapper clones raw IDs before the product method may rewrite them, calls the original prepare method once, and emits no equality success after a fallback or product exception.
Runtime installation rejects non-CUDA cache devices; successful evidence rejects CPU resident banks and labels only CUDA resident rows.
Six Triton NVFP4 bank roles, their expected dtypes, per-row geometry, consumed full-slot GEMM views, raw-to-slot mapping, and inverse slot ownership are all checked.
Every selected source/resident row is compared as uint8 bytes; source/resident digests are emitted in sorted unique-expert order; temporary resident gathering is bounded to eight expert rows.
The observer explicitly does not infer physical H2D bytes or collect timing/performance.
coverage_gaps: The CPU fixture covers two selected experts only, so it does not execute the greater-than-eight-expert chunk loop.
Per-bank corruption tests alter selected resident slot 4 only; add a case corrupting the other selected slot 0 so a one-row-only implementation cannot pass.
No test binds wrapper context to an actual scheduler/D0 prefill segment or verifies the selected 64/233/123 request history.

Context must bind UID and actual layer-major child extent, not only outer segment_index: engine.forward_batch disables layer-major when route_tracer is present, and historical tracer segment denominators are not a guarantee for a trace-off candidate.
CPU protocol tests use synthetic CPU bank tensors; CUDA/NVFP4 copy kernel, pinned host allocation, actual cache lifecycle, model numerical equivalence, SSE output, and performance remain unvalidated.
limits: This review accepts the diagnostic observer's CPU protocol implementation only.
It does not admit D12, establish transfer timing or physical PCIe behavior, prove fixed-logit/state/SSE equivalence, or validate the enabled threshold path on GPU.
